Class ChecksumCodec

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.transform.checksum.ChecksumCodec
All Implemented Interfaces:
Codec<byte[]>
public final class ChecksumCodec extends Object implements Codec<byte[]>
A Codec<byte[]> transform that appends a 32-bit checksum (big-endian) on encode and verifies it on decode, rejecting a mismatch with InvalidPayloadException. It detects accidental corruption — bit rot, a truncated write, a partially overwritten cache entry — so that damaged bytes fail here instead of confusing a parser downstream or decoding to a plausible but wrong value.

It is not tamper-proof: anyone who can change the bytes can recompute the checksum. Encrypted payloads from codec-crypto are already authenticated and gain nothing from this; gzip, Zstandard and LZ4 frames carry their own checksums. The realistic use is an uncompressed, unencrypted payload such as plain JSON in a cache.

crc32c() is the recommended form: CRC-32C has better error-detection properties than CRC-32 or Adler-32 and a dedicated CPU instruction on common hardware. Any other 32-bit Checksum — CRC32, Adler32, or a custom one — can be supplied for interoperability. Checksum.getValue() returns a long only because Java has no unsigned int; a checksum whose value does not fit in 32 bits is rejected rather than truncated.

Instances are immutable and thread-safe; a fresh Checksum is taken from the supplier per operation.
